parameters.query: SELECT business_id FROM vaibhavcapstone_businesses ORDER BY business_id;

SELECT
 b.business_id, b.name AS business_name,
 b.config->>'reviewer_email' AS reviewer_email, b.config->>'sender_identity' AS sender_identity,
 jsonb_build_object(
  'week_start', (now() - interval '7 days')::date,
  'week_end', now()::date,
  'volume_total', (SELECT count(*) FROM vaibhavcapstone_leads l WHERE l.business_id = b.business_id AND l.received_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
  'daily', (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('day', to_char(d, 'Dy DD Mon'), 'count', c) ORDER BY d), '[]'::jsonb)
            FROM (SELECT date_trunc('day', received_at) d, count(*) c FROM vaibhavcapstone_leads
                  WHERE business_id = b.business_id AND received_at > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY 1) t),
  'band_mix', (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_object_agg(band, c), '{}'::jsonb)
               FROM (SELECT q.band, count(*) c FROM vaibhavcapstone_qualifications q JOIN vaibhavcapstone_leads l USING (lead_id)
                     WHERE q.business_id = b.business_id AND l.received_at > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY q.band) t),
  'status_mix', (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_object_agg(status, c), '{}'::jsonb)
                 FROM (SELECT status, count(*) c FROM vaibhavcapstone_leads
                       WHERE business_id = b.business_id AND received_at > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY status) t),
  'funnel', jsonb_build_object(
    'received', (SELECT count(*) FROM vaibhavcapstone_leads l WHERE l.business_id = b.business_id AND l.received_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
    'enquiries', (SELECT count(*) FROM vaibhavcapstone_extractions e JOIN vaibhavcapstone_leads l USING (lead_id) WHERE e.business_id = b.business_id AND e.classification = 'ENQUIRY' AND l.received_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
    'qualified', (SELECT count(*) FROM vaibhavcapstone_qualifications q JOIN vaibhavcapstone_leads l USING (lead_id) WHERE q.business_id = b.business_id AND l.received_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
    'recommended', (SELECT count(*) FROM vaibhavcapstone_recommendations r JOIN vaibhavcapstone_leads l USING (lead_id) WHERE r.business_id = b.business_id AND r.grounded AND l.received_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
    'sent', (SELECT count(*) FROM vaibhavcapstone_leads l WHERE l.business_id = b.business_id AND l.status = 'SENT' AND l.received_at > now() - interval '7 days')),
  'approval', (SELECT jsonb_build_object('approved', count(*) FILTER (WHERE action = 'DRAFT_APPROVED'),
                                          'rejected', count(*) FILTER (WHERE action = 'DRAFT_REJECTED'))
               FROM vaibhavcapstone_events WHERE business_id = b.business_id AND created_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
  'avg_mins_to_draft', (SELECT round((avg(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (d.created_at - r2.created_at)) / 60))::numeric, 1)
                        FROM vaibhavcapstone_events r2 JOIN vaibhavcapstone_events d
                          ON d.lead_id = r2.lead_id AND d.action = 'DRAFT_CREATED'
                        WHERE r2.action = 'LEAD_RECEIVED' AND r2.business_id = b.business_id AND r2.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
  'needs_review', (SELECT count(*) FROM vaibhavcapstone_leads l WHERE l.business_id = b.business_id AND l.status = 'NEEDS_REVIEW' AND l.received_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
  'top_categories', (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('category', cat, 'count', c) ORDER BY c DESC), '[]'::jsonb)
                     FROM (SELECT p.category cat, count(*) c FROM vaibhavcapstone_recommendations rec CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(rec.items) i JOIN vaibhavcapstone_products p ON p.sku = i->>'sku' AND p.business_id = rec.business_id
                           WHERE rec.business_id = b.business_id AND rec.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'
                           GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5) t),
  'ai_health', jsonb_build_object(
    'llm_calls', (SELECT count(*) FROM vaibhavcapstone_llm_calls c WHERE c.business_id = b.business_id AND c.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
    'cost_per_lead_usd', (SELECT round((COALESCE(sum(c.cost_usd),0) / GREATEST((SELECT count(*) FROM vaibhavcapstone_leads l2 WHERE l2.business_id = b.business_id AND l2.received_at > now() - interval '7 days'),1))::numeric, 5)
        FROM vaibhavcapstone_llm_calls c WHERE c.business_id = b.business_id AND c.created_at > now() - interval '7 days' AND c.call_site <> 'judge' AND c.usage_source = 'exact_api'),
    'latency_p50_ms', (SELECT percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY c.latency_ms) FROM vaibhavcapstone_llm_calls c WHERE c.business_id = b.business_id AND c.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
    'latency_p95_ms', (SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY c.latency_ms) FROM vaibhavcapstone_llm_calls c WHERE c.business_id = b.business_id AND c.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
    'schema_validity_pct', (SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.schema_valid) / GREATEST(count(*),1), 1) FROM vaibhavcapstone_llm_calls c WHERE c.business_id = b.business_id AND c.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
    'retries', (SELECT count(*) FROM vaibhavcapstone_llm_calls c WHERE c.business_id = b.business_id AND c.attempt > 1 AND c.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
    'fallbacks', (SELECT count(*) FROM vaibhavcapstone_llm_calls c WHERE c.business_id = b.business_id AND c.fallback_used AND c.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
    'judge', (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_object_agg(t.artifact_type, jsonb_build_object('avg', t.avg, 'n', t.n, 'violations', t.v)), '{}'::jsonb)
      FROM (SELECT artifact_type, round(avg(score),2) AS avg, count(*) AS n,
                   sum(jsonb_array_length(violations)) AS v
            FROM vaibhavcapstone_judge_scores j WHERE j.business_id = b.business_id AND j.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'
            GROUP BY artifact_type) t)
  )
 ) AS metrics
FROM vaibhavcapstone_businesses b WHERE b.business_id = $1;

parameters.content:
## The Monday morning report

Every Monday at 8am each business gets an email showing how its enquiries are going: how many arrived, how they scored, how quickly they were answered — and what the AI cost to run.

Every number is computed from that business's own records. **The AI is only allowed to write the commentary around the figures, never to produce a figure.**

### Who gets a report, and when

**Three ways in.** Monday at 8am automatically; a "run now" address used for demos; and a third, separate address for reading the latest report in a browser — that's the lane underneath.

**Fetch the businesses, then handle them one at a time.** Each gets its own report built from its own data. Nobody ever sees anyone else's numbers.

### Reading the latest report in a browser

A small separate path with nothing to do with Monday: ask for a business's most recently stored report and show it as a web page.

Handy for demos — and for anyone who deleted the email.

### Work out the numbers

**One big question to the database** produces the whole picture: how many enquiries arrived, how they split across hot, warm and cold, how many reached a reply, how long each stage took, and what every AI call cost.

Asking it as a *single* question matters — every figure then comes from the same instant, so no two parts of the report can disagree with each other.

**Turn the numbers into charts.** Email programs won't run code, so a chart can't be drawn inside the message. Each chart is built as a web address that returns a picture, and the email simply shows those pictures.

### Let the AI write the words — never the numbers

**The AI is handed the finished figures** and asked for a short, readable summary. It is never asked to work anything out; every number is already fixed before it sees them.

Google's AI first, OpenAI as backup, both answers flattened to one shape — and the call recorded with its exact tokens and cost, which is itself one of the numbers in next week's report.

**If the AI writes nothing usable, the report still goes out**, with a plain line saying the summary isn't available this week. Every figure and chart is still there. The commentary is a nicety; the data is the point.

### Store it, send it, next business

**Save the finished report** so it can be re-read later at the "latest report" address without building it again.

**Email it to the business**, then loop back and do the whole thing for the next one.

## Why you can trust every number in this report

**Every figure here can be re-derived by hand from the records.**

The AI writes sentences, never numbers. The figures all come from one question asked at one moment. And the section reporting what the AI itself cost is computed exactly like everything else.

That rule earned its keep during the build: it caught the report's own AI call landing *after* its own snapshot, so the report was never counting itself.
